answer: Proof-of-replication resists Sybil attacks by having each agent seal a dataset with a slow, key-dependent sequential encoding and answer random Merkle challenges faster than re-sealing allows. Because distinct replicas cannot be deduplicated across keys, attackers cannot grow a Sybil garden on shared disks or cycle clones like a comet, paying dedicated disk space and copper bus I/O per identity. However, sealing delays newcomers and bulk storage farms can still scale linearly.
